title: WPSS/1615/2013 of Smt Nirmala Kotnala Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No.1615 of 2013 (S/S)
Smt. Nirmala Kotnala. ..Ö..Petitioner

Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others. ÖÖ.Respondents
 And
Writ Petition No.1616 of 2013 (S/S)
Smt. Rajeshwari Tiwari. ..Ö..Petitioner

Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others. ÖÖ.Respondents
Mr. B.D. Upadhyaya, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Naveen Tewari, Advocate for the
petitioners.
Mr. Subhash Upadhyaya, Standing Counsel for the State.

Dated: October 24, 2013
Honíble V.K. Bist, J.
Controversy involved in these petitions is identical
therefore, the writ petitions are consolidated and are being
decided by a common judgment. Writ Petiton No.1615 of
2013 (S/S) shall be the leading case.
2. During the course of argument, learned Senior
Advocate for the petitioners submitted that he is confining
to the challenge of the order, by which the attachment
order of the petitioners have been cancelled. Rest of the
prayers are not pressed.
3. It is contended by the learned Senior Advocate for the
petitioners that earlier in the year 2010, the petitioners
were transferred from one School to another subject to
availability of posts. Though, at that time, posts were not

2
available, but subsequently, posts in the concerned schools
fell vacant. Thereafter, another order was passed by the
respondent authority making attachment of the petitioners
in that school. According to the learned counsel for the
petitioners, this order was not correct order and in fact, the
petitioners should have been treated as transferred in that
institution. Now, by the order impugned, the attachment
order of the petitioners has been cancelled.
4. The main contention of the learned Senior Advocate
for the petitioners is that the respondents have acted
illegally by treating the petitioners attached to that
institution. He argued that in fact, the petitioners joined
the said posts against the vacant post on transfer.
5. Mr. Subhash Upadhyaya, Standing Counsel for the
State submitted that in fact, the petitioners accepted the
attachment orders and now, at this stage, they cannot
challenge the said orders. He submitted that there is
provision under Rule 26 of the Transfer rules under which
the petitioners can file appeal.
6. In rejoinder reply, the learned Senior Advocate
submitted that the petitioners have already completed more
than five years in the institution and in such view of the
matter; the petitioners could have been transferred to other
schools. He argued that the petitioners have no objection in
case regular transfer order is passed. He submitted that in
the name of attachment, petitioners cannot be sent back to
the original School.
7. Considering the submission advanced by the learned
counsel for the parties, the writ petitions are disposed of by

3
permitting the petitioners to submit representations before
the competent authority within one week. In case such
representations are filed by the petitioners within the
stipulated period, the competent authority shall take
decision on the representations of the petitioners, in
accordance with law, within a period of ten daysí from the
date of filing of representations along with the certified copy
of this order. While deciding the representations, it will be
open for the respondents to pass fresh transfer order of the
petitioners. Till the representations filed by the petitioners
are decided, the order impugned (so far same relate to the
petitioners), shall be kept in abeyance. The respondents are
also directed to make payment of salary to the petitioners.

8. Interim relief applications also stand disposed of.
9. No order as to costs.
10. Let a copy of this judgment be placed in the
connected writ petition.
11. Let a certified copy of this order be supplied to the
learned counsel for the parties within 24 hours on payment
of usual charges.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
Arpan 24.10.2013
